The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 116 - 115, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday evening. The Magic jumped out to a quick 90 lead and went ahead to push it to a 26 - 10 advantage with 4:55 left in the first. However, the Sixers battled back and cut the gap to just two points, trailing, 32 - 30, after one. The 76ers pulled ahead in the second carried the lead for most of the quarter, before taking a 63 - 52 lead into halftime. The tides turned again in the third quarter, as the Magic outscored the 76ers by eight, to cut the deficit to three points, heading into the final frame. The Sixers maintained their edge and pushed the lead back to 10, with five minutes to go in the game, but the Magic used an 18 - 9 run to make it a one - point game with 5 seconds left and possession. The Magic were not able to convert on the final play and dropped their second game in as many nights. On the other hand, the Sixers earned their second straight win. Joel Embiid led Philadelphia with 32 points, 10 rebounds and three assists, in 33 minutes. J.J. Redick came up huge in 32 minutes off the bench, with 31 points, four rebounds and four assists. Dario Saric finished with 13 points, nine rebounds, five assists, one block and one steal, while Robert Covington added 12 points, four rebounds, two steals, one block and one assist. The Sixers shot 48 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Evan Fournier was the high - point man for the Magic with 31 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal, in 33 minutes. Nikola Vucevic had a big night with 27 points, 13 rebounds, 12 assists and two steals, in 37 minutes of action, while Aaron Gordon finished with 20 points, 12 rebounds three assists, three blocks and one steal. The Magic shot 46 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 29 from distance. The Magic (1 - 2) take on the Celtics in Boston on Monday, while the 76ers, head to Detroit to challenge the Pistons on Tuesday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 105 - 103, at Wells Fargo Center on Saturday evening. The battle of two evenly matched teams was as good as expected, as neither club gave an inch through four quarters. A see - saw first half saw the 76ers (3 - 3) enter halftime holding a slim 63 - 62 advantage. Ultimately, a standout defensive effort by Philadelphia that saw them limit the Hornets (3 - 4) to 18 points in the final period helped key the hard - fought win. Both teams scuffled from the field with Charlotte's 39 percent success rate only slightly exceeding the Sixers' 38 percent figure. However, the home squad enjoyed a strong rebounding advantage, winning the battle of the boards by a 56 - 48 margin. Kemba Walker paced the Hornets with a game - high 37 points, a total he supplemented with six rebounds, six assists, two blocks and one steal. Miles Bridges followed with a bench - leading 14 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds and one steal. Cody Zeller produced 12 points, six boards and one steal, while Jeremy Lamb matched his point total and added three rebounds and one assist. Joel Embiid led the way for the Sixers with a 27 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and two blocks. Robert Covington generated an 18 - point, 10 - rebound double - double of his own. J.J. Redick poured in 15 point to lead the second unit. Ben Simmons supplied 14 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and one steal. Dario Saric contributed 11 points, seven rebounds and one assist. Markelle Fultz turned in 10 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Hornets head back home and await a visit from the Miami Heat on Tuesday night, while the 76ers remain home to take on the Atlanta Hawks on Monday evening.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 113 - 92, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday night. The 76ers (4 - 3) kept their undefeated run at home alive with a convincing win over the Hawks (2 - 4), as Atlanta fought hard but ultimately didn't have enough in them to battle with Philadelphia. In fact, Atlanta won the first quarter 25 - 20, but Philadelphia evened things up with a 27 - 22 second quarter that kept the score tied at 47 after the first two quarters. Philadelphia showed a bit of their playoff form last season with an impressive 31 - 13 third quarter, and they later closed things out with a 35 - 32 fourth quarter. Without a doubt, it was a strong showing from the Sixers and now they move up to 40 at home. Ben Simmons was the star of the game for Philadelphia and he came one assist short of a triple - double thanks to a 21 - point, 12 - rebound, nine - assist stat line, while Joel Embiid registered 10 points, six rebounds, six assists and two blocks. Markelle Fultz chipped in with 16 points and seven assists, Robert Covington added 11 points with six rebounds, and three bench players reached the 10 - point mark: J.J. Redick (14), Mike Muscala (14) and Landry Shamet (13). Kent Bazemore had 18 points to led all players for the Hawks, while rookie point guard Trae Young contributed with 11 points and eight assists. Dewayne Dedmon and Omari Spellman each chipped in with 11 points coming off the bench for the Hawks. All 13 Atlanta players scored, but only four reached the 10 - point mark.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 133 - 132, in overtime at Wells Fargo Center on Friday evening. The 76ers (8 - 5) found themselves at the scene of the majority of their successes Friday, as they'd come into the contest with a perfect 60 record at home. After a nip - and - tuck first quarter, Philadelphia seemingly turned the game in their favor with a 32 - 17 advantage in the second period. Cody Zeller matched Hernangomez's scoring and rebounding totals, while Michael Kidd-Gilchrist generated a 12 - point, 12 - rebound double - double off the bench. Embiid led the Sixers with a 42 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and four blocks. Ben Simmons tallied a 22 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included eight boards, three blocks and two steals. Dario Saric contributed 18 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. J.J. Redick finished with 17 points, four assists and two rebounds. Markelle Fultz and Robert Covington started but only had seven points each. The Hornets remain on the road and take on the Pistons on Sunday afternoon, while the 76ers pay a visit to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 116 - 102, at Wells Fargo Center on Monday evening. The Pistons jumped to an early, 7 - 4, lead but the 76ers came back to tie it at 11, four minutes into the first quarter. The Sixers did not look back from there, as they used a quick, 90, run to create some separation, and held on to take a, 38 - 29, lead into the second quarter. However, the 76ers charged back with a, 11 - 3, run to bring a, 87 - 76, lead into the final frame. The 76ers cruised from there to their second win in a row, while the Pistons dropped their fifth in a row. Ben Simmons followed up with 18 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one block, while T.J. McConnell added 14 points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals, in 28 minutes off the bench. Luke Kennard had a big night for the Pistons, with 28 points, eight rebounds and three assists, in 36 minutes. Blake Griffin (rest) did not suit up, but Andre Drummond finished with 21 points, 17 rebounds, three blocks, two assists and one steal. In fact, the Sixers won each of the first three quarters by at least three points apiece, as they led by 17 heading into the fourth quarter. Dallas did respond with a 30 - 19 fourth quarter, as that got the lead down to four points with less than a minute remaining. Defense was critical for the Sixers, as they held the Mavericks to 43 percent from the field, 29 percent from three - point range and 65 percent from the free - throw line. Philadelphia did a ton of work down low too, outscoring the Mavericks in the paint, 62 - 52. Philly's starters really dominated Dallas's starters, outscoring them, 83 - 49. The Mavericks (18 - 21) are now 3 - 18 on the road this season, as this marks their 10th loss in their last 13 games in total. Wesley Matthews was their leading scorer in this game, as he finished with 18 points and two rebounds. Luka Doncic tallied 14 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two steals. Jalen Brunson was huge off the bench, providing 13 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists. The Sixers (26 - 14) were led by Joel Embiid, as he collected 25 points, 12 rebounds and five assists. J.J. Redick amassed 20 points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals. Ben Simmons accumulated 20 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists en route to a triple - double. Jonah Bolden got a rare start and accrued 11 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two blocks. On deck for Dallas is a home matchup versus the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday. As for Philly, they play host to the Washington Wizards on Tuesday for their next outing.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Washington Wizards, 132 - 115, at Wells Fargo Center on Tuesday evening. The Wizards (16 - 25) came out of the gates ready to do battle against their superior conference opponent, but the 76ers (27 - 14) bounced back from an early 20 - 12 deficit to close out the first quarter on a 20 - 9 run that would set the tone for more dominance to come. Philadelphia went on to outscore Washington by a 36 - 16 margin in the second quarter to secure a dominating advantage that they wouldn't relinquish. The Wizards shot well (51 percent), but the Sixers were just a bit better at 56 percent, including 52 percent from three - point range. Meanwhile, the home squad won the battle of the boards handily by a 49 - 34 margin. Bradley Beal paced the Wizards with 28 points and added three rebounds, two assists and three steals. Jeff Green followed with 15 points, a rebound, an assist and a steal. Sam Dekker led a productive bench effort with 14 points, four assists, three rebounds and two steals. Otto Porter, Jr. mustered 11 points, while Ian Mahinmi and Chasson Randle generated matched 10 - point tallies. Mahinmi notably pulled down seven rebounds and dished out five assists as well. Landry Shamet led the Sixers with 29 points off the bench, supplementing them with three rebounds, one assist and one steal. Joel Embiid produced a 20 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and one block. Jimmy Butler supplied 20 points, five rebounds, three assists and two steals. Ben Simmons totaled 17 points, nine assists, five boards and three steals. Furkan Korkmaz drew the start for J.J. Redick (back) and managed 16 points. The two teams meet again on Wednesday night in the Nation's Capital for the second game of the home - and - home set.
